Rust crates compiled into pytakumi 0.1.5
========================================================================

The pytakumi 0.1.5 wheels (cp314, manylinux_2_28, x86_64 and aarch64) carry
a CycloneDX SBOM, pytakumi-0.1.5.dist-info/sboms/pytakumi.cyclonedx.json,
written by cargo-cyclonedx 0.5.9, which is the same for both architectures.
It lists 171 crates as required: Takumi's six crates, built from the copy of
Takumi 2.14.0 vendored in the pytakumi source (texts:
takumi-2.14.0.LICENSE-MIT and takumi-2.14.0.LICENSE-APACHE), and the 165
crates.io crates below. It lists 14 more as build tools only; they are not
here.

Each crate's archive was fetched from
https://static.crates.io/crates/<name>/<name>-<version>.crate and matched the
sha256 recorded in pytakumi's Cargo.lock. The texts are every LICENSE,
LICENCE, COPYING, COPYRIGHT, NOTICE, PATENTS, AUTHORS and UNLICENSE file at
the top of each archive, and the COPYING and PATENTS of the libwebp C library
that libwebp-sys compiles in. Texts that are the same apart from line endings
and trailing spaces are given once, under the list of crates that carry them.
No archive carries a NOTICE file.

Three archives carry no licence file. taffy 0.14.0 and wuff 0.2.8 (both MIT):
their LICENSE is taken from the commit each archive was packaged from (its
.cargo_vcs_info.json), at github.com/DioxusLabs/taffy and
github.com/nicoburns/wuff. selectors 0.40.0 (MPL-2.0): the MPL-2.0 text, as
cssparser carries it. libwebp-sys 0.14.4 declares MIT for its own code and
publishes no licence text, in the archive or upstream
(github.com/NoXF/libwebp-sys has none at the packaged commit).

The required list also holds crates whose code never reaches the binary:
procedural macros and the crates they use, which run inside the compiler
(syn, quote, proc-macro2, serde_derive and the like), and crates for other
systems (windows-link, redox_syscall). Their texts are carried anyway.

Four crates are MPL-2.0 only: cssparser 0.37.0, cssparser-macros 0.7.0,
dtoa-short 0.3.5 and selectors 0.40.0. No file in their archives applies the
"Incompatible With Secondary Licenses" notice (the phrase appears only in the
licence text itself). Their source is the archive at the URL above, for
each name and version.
